A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Meta Flow Matching with the same authors, central method, and applications. Their text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic letter-denoising experiments and organoid treatment-response evaluations, including numerical comparisons and culture-specific appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds patient-holdout evaluations, OT comparisons, a training-population ablation, and embedding and treatment-prediction analyses.

M1.justification: The GNN-conditioned vector field, MFM objective, architecture, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. V2 adds an evaluated MFMw/OT variant for synthetic letters (Table 4), using optimal-transport couplings instead of independent pairing during training. This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate letter denoising and treatment-response prediction on the same organoid dataset covering ten patients, eleven treatments, and three culture conditions. Additional patient holdouts, rotation counts, and analyses change protocols or evidence within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 retains FM, CGFM, and ICNN and adds evaluated FMw/OT and CGFMw/OT comparisons. Organoid tables also introduce unchanged-source and training-mean-shift baselines, plus a training-only true-target-mean diagnostic. These additions substantially strengthen the comparator set beyond v1's learned baselines.

E3.justification: V1's 861-training/33-test 'patient' setting is reclassified as replica-2, which permits other replicates from that patient in training. V2 separately evaluates complete holdouts of PDO-21, PDO-27, and PDO-75 (Appendix D.2). Reported synthetic training budgets change from 2000/4000 to 12000/24000 epochs for FM/CGFM versus MFM, despite unchanged Table 1 values. New experiments vary training-population counts and coupling procedures. Appendix D.3 also describes r² through pairwise correlations rather than v1's mean-feature squared correlation; these reporting changes do not establish that retained results were recomputed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained neighborhood-size and Gaussian-source comparisons, v2 adds training-population sensitivity (Figure 5), independent-versus-OT coupling analysis (Table 4), population-embedding visualization and clustering (Figure 7), and treatment-specific prediction case studies (Figure 8). These address substantially more questions about generalization and learned representations.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and numerical uncertainty. V2 additionally reports means and standard deviations across three patient holdouts in Tables 3 and 7, introducing between-split variability reporting. This does not establish an increase in the seed count.

E6.justification: Table 1 and most original flow-model organoid values are retained, but v2 adds patient-holdout, OT, ablation, embedding, and treatment-analysis results. ICNN entries also change: replica-1 fibroblast test W1 changes from 3.828 to 3.784 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 8). In v2's new patient evaluation, FMw/OT achieves W1 4.064 versus 4.087 for MFM with k=50 (Table 3). These new patient aggregates are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds Appendix A's formal measure-space definitions and refines the tangent-space description using an L2 closure. Appendix D.3 also supplies a different formal r² construction from v1's description. Proposition 1, Theorem 1, and its proof otherwise remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: amortizing flow matching over initial populations, learning population embeddings with a GNN, generalizing to unseen distributions, and predicting patient-specific treatment responses. Additional evaluations support and qualify these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 replaces blanket baseline-failure language with a more qualified account of MFM's competitiveness against OT methods. New appendix interpretations connect embeddings to patient chemosensitivity and predicted treatment patterns to Oxaliplatin response. V2 also discusses biological heterogeneity across replicas and identifies biological MFM-with-OT evaluation as future work. These substantially expand the interpretation of the empirical evidence.

D1.justification: V2 adds evaluation sample limits, MMD kernel parameters, synthetic batch sizes, explicit validation counts, and UMAP/PCA analysis procedures. A new reproducibility statement reports supplementary code submission. V1 already documented the principal architectures, optimizers, software, hardware, runtimes, and the same public repository.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liu et al. (2022a, 2024) on generalized Schrödinger bridges and distinguishes their interacting terms from generalization to unseen distributions. It refines the discussion of ICNN generalization and population-level novelty, and removes the Gretton et al. (2012) citation. Most research positioning is retained; duplicate-reference cleanup and publication-metadata changes are not new works.

P1.justification: V2 revises experimental exposition, adds descriptive paragraph headings and a reproducibility statement, merges limitations with future work, and moves broader impacts and the neighborhood-size discussion into appendices. The introduction, background, method narrative, and main section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, adds Figures 5, 7, and 8, and restructures biological results into compact test-only main tables with fuller appendix tables and OT/non-OT formatting. It also introduces shaded mathematical statement boxes and a conference layout. Earlier letter visualizations are retained, including v1 Figure 5 becoming v2 Figure 6.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central generalization claim: it distinguishes the old patient-labeled results as replica-2 and separately reports three complete patient holdouts, competitive OT baselines, and simple controls. The added ablations and biological analyses make the method's behavior more assessable and its performance interpretation better calibrated. These gains outweigh remaining reporting ambiguities, particularly the changed training budgets alongside unchanged Table 1 scores and the inconsistent descriptions of r².
